analysis.title: GS flow and positioning observations
key_insights: Markets bounced after weekend Asian support measures: China lowered margin requirements, Korea eased buyback restrictions, Taiwan tightened short-selling rules. Privorotsky calls these sticking plasters that are not what you want to see at a bottom.

Trump administration comments supportive of Nvidia (Bessent on CNBC and CBS) separate compute sales to China from supplying the military and leave the door open to Jensen's return, conditional on the compliance investigation. Desk warns a rhetorical pivot is not regulatory relief, and the real test is licenses for offshore data centers.

Pasquariello: NVDA shed $2.7tr of market cap over six weeks and accounts for most of the S&P breakdown from the Oct 6 highs through Nov 11. The AI leaders basket is now down on the year after being up 53% YTD five months ago.

Hedge fund de-risking is very large. Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 3.1 pts to 42.3% (1st percentile 1-year) and beta-adjusted net leverage fell 8.8 pts to 48.2% (5-year low). Shorting was the largest since April 2025, and US single stocks were shorted every day last week.

Vol hit panic extremes: VIX approached 40, GS Vol Panic Index 9.8 of 10, VXN highest since COVID, VXSMH at an all-time high, and the VIX curve most inverted since April 2025. Historical analogs (Oct 08, May 10, Feb 20, Apr 25) show average SPX returns of +5.9% over 3 months and +26.5% over 1 year.

Coppersmith cautions that panic readings above 9 in a hiking regime averaged just +0.4% three-month returns, and Oct 2018 panic was followed by another 6.8% decline. Broad investor positioning has not washed out: GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator sits at the 75th percentile, with about $170bn of equity fund inflows since Q4 start.

Desk prefers underwriting vol over chasing stocks. Coppersmith favors selling puts at levels where they would add length, especially in tech where vol repricing is most extreme. Pasquariello's instinct is the volatility high for this episode has been seen.

Garrett recommends long delta with net short or vega-flat footprints: window knock-outs, VIX calendar put spreads (+Dec p / sell Jan p), knock-out calls on baskets or singles, and short puts in most convicted longs. He agrees with Ben Snider that hyperscalers are the vol-adjusted best place for capital.
Six-week straddle price rose from 4% to 8.2%, with the 6-week breakeven (~8%) equal to the long-run annualized equity return. One-month variance prices almost 250bps daily moves through Christmas.

CTAs sold $57bn of US equities over the past month and flipped net short. Selling risk now sits mostly outside the US, and US CTAs would be buyers on a bounce. Dealer gamma is negative and SPX top-of-book liquidity is about $4mm, near YTD lows, into a shortened Thanksgiving week.

Option volume exploded: Friday was the 4th largest session ever at 104.5mm contracts, and NVDA made up 30% of SPX-constituent option volume (9.1mm of 30mm). NVDA rallied 3.7% post close Friday after November expiry.

Rates view: Privorotsky argues the Fed is mispriced given the growth shock, commodity collapse, low inflation expectations, tight financial conditions and high real rates. He expects an outsized reaction when the first FOMC member acknowledges tightening, and notes Bessent has raised the risk of a Fed policy mistake.

Parallels to Nov/Dec 2018 are drawn. High-beta cyclicals are +12% YTD versus US AI negative, and in 4Q18 cyclicals fell 23% and lagged SPX by 10pp. At 15x forward P/E they trade at a roughly 40% premium to the 2018 trough multiple.

Valuation reset: S&P P/E fell from 22x at start of year to 16x, below the 30-year average, and NDX is at its lowest multiple of the COVID/post-COVID era. GS Research frames SPX outcomes between about 5,800 and 8,100.
Credit is the tell: if Nvidia rallies while neocloud spreads stay under pressure, the move is likely short covering. AI infrastructure depends on external capital as its cost rises.
Event calendar: Flash PMIs Monday, Dell earnings Tuesday, Beige Book and Core PCE Wednesday, then payrolls, December FOMC and November CPI. Shortened US week may amplify squeezes.

Still +12% YTD at 15x forward P/E, about 40% above the 2018 trough, and fell 23% in 4Q18.
Garrett agrees with Snider that they are the vol-adjusted best place for capital under both AI payback scenarios.

risk_factors: Nvidia policy pivot is rhetorical, with investigations and remote access restrictions still active.
Broad investor positioning has not washed out, with sentiment indicator at the 75th percentile and strong fund inflows.
Hiking Fed with no Fed put, and a 2018-style second leg lower.
Thin liquidity and negative dealer gamma in a shortened Thanksgiving week.
AI financing and oversupply, with neocloud credit spreads under pressure.
Core PCE and November CPI could shift Fed expectations.
vol_and_positioning: VIX approached 40, VIX curve at steepest inversion since April 2025, CNN Fear & Greed around 10, put/call ratios near 95th percentile.
GS Vol Panic Index 9.8 of 10. Readings above 9.5 historically signaled near-term relief.
Weekly VIX increase was the 5th largest on record. Past comparable spikes averaged SPX +5.1% next day, +3.3% next week, +5.9% next 3 months, +26.5% next year.
VXN highest since COVID, VXSMH all-time high, six-week straddle from 4% to 8.2%.
Fundamental L/S gross leverage 204.8% (13th percentile), net 42.3% (1st percentile 1-year), beta-adjusted net 48.2% (5-year low). Momentum exposure fell from a record +70% in June to negative.
HF VIP basket GSTHHVIP lagged SPX by 14pp over six months. Fundamental L/S lost 1.2% Friday and is down 2.1% MTD, while systematic L/S is up 1.5%.
CTAs sold $57bn over the month and are net short. NDX CTA positioning is near the bottom of its 10-year range.
Friday option volume was 104.5mm contracts. The 29 names with Mon/Wed/Fri expiries are realizing 82 vol. ETF share of tape exceeded 39%.
Dealer gamma is negative and SPX top-of-book liquidity is about $4mm.
geopolitical: China lowered margin requirements, Korea eased buyback restrictions, Taiwan tightened short selling rules over the weekend.
Nvidia export restrictions to China, remote compute access, and TSMC licensing uncertainty. Bessent distinguishes compute sales to China from military supply.
Trump administration public support for Jensen Huang's reinstatement, conditional on a compliance investigation.

tension_points.bull_case: Extreme vol, HF net leverage at 1st percentile, CTAs short US equities, and VIX above 35 historically preceded rebounds, with SPX at 16x P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: Broad positioning not washed out (sentiment indicator at 75th percentile, ~$170bn inflows), Fed hiking, and Oct 2018 panic was followed by a further 6.8% decline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nvidia rallies while neocloud credit spreads stay under pressure, signaling only short covering, or a hot Core PCE or November CPI print.

theme_stances.key_argument: Extreme positioning, vol and a potential Nvidia policy pivot create a compelling tactical setup.
Vol has overshot without needing to call an equity bottom, so underwriting vol beats chasing stocks.
theme_stances.evidence: we'd rather be underwriting some of this volatility than chasing stocks
